prompt.brief: Design an automated model-retraining platform that responds to schedules, drift, and new labels, builds reproducible candidates, applies quality and safety gates, and promotes or rolls back approved models.
successSignals: Define retraining triggers, point-in-time datasets, labels/cutoffs, experiment lineage, evaluation gates, approvals, artifact versions, and rollback.
Prevent leakage and accidental promotion; compare candidates against production on quality, calibration, fairness, latency, cost, and safety metrics.
Separate trigger detection, data preparation, training, validation, shadow/canary serving, and promotion; make every stage resumable and idempotent.
Explain drift storms, missing labels, reproducibility, privacy, resource quotas, auditability, observability, and last-known-good fallback.

functional: Trigger runs from schedules, drift, or new labels; snapshot data, train candidates, evaluate gates, register artifacts, and request approval.
Deploy shadow/canary candidates, compare live outcomes, promote or roll back, and expose lineage, metrics, owner, status, and model freshness.
Support cancellation, deduplicated triggers, data deletion, reproducible replay, resource quotas, failed-run recovery, and model retirement.
nonFunctional: Complete standard retraining within four hours and never replace the production model without passing mandatory gates and approval policy.
Run thousands of model pipelines with burst isolation without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 5k models, 1k concurrent training runs, and daily plus drift triggers
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Automated model-retraining platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Automated model-retraining platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Automated model-retraining platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Automated model-retraining platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Automated model-retraining platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Automated model-retraining platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Automated model-retraining platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Automated model-retraining platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Automated model-retraining platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
